services.label: Three scenarios
services.headline: Three service routes
services.description: The service route is defined after the initial equipment assessment. Repairs, price, and lead time are approved before work begins.
services.s1_desc: We accept a working instrument, check completeness, arrange verification with an accredited organization, and control the procedure.
services.s1_result: A working instrument and the required verification results.
services.s2_desc: We inspect sensors, pumps, power, electronics, and gas response. Before repair, we report the findings, price, and lead time.
services.s2_result: An approved scope of work and diagnostic findings.
services.s3_desc: We accept batches, record composition and status, distribute work by stage, and help plan future deadlines.
services.s3_result: Status and deadline for every instrument.
services.s4_desc: We adjust sensitivity and reading correctness using gas mixtures, checking response and measurement stability.
services.s5_desc: We help prepare instruments and documents for internal audits, inspections, and industrial safety requirements.
services.s6_desc: We build regular verification and service schedules so gas analyzers do not drop out of operation unexpectedly.
services.cta: Discuss the task with an engineer

process.label: Work process
process.title: How an order is processed
process.description: We record the initial condition and never start additional work without approval.
process.step1_text: We record the model, serial number, completeness, appearance, and the customer task.
process.step2_text: We check startup, power, sensors, pump, and response to a test gas mixture.
process.step3_text: We report diagnostics, price, and lead time, and begin repair only after confirmation.
process.step4_text: We arrange verification of the working instrument with an accredited organization and monitor the outcome.
process.step5_text: We return instruments, documents, and recommendations for further operation and service.

faq.label: FAQ
faq.headline: What to know before gas analyzer verification
faq.description: Short answers to questions that affect the timing, price, and document package.
faq.q1: Can you tell whether repair is needed before verification?
faq.a1: Usually this is clear after initial diagnostics. If self-test fails, readings are unstable, or the instrument does not respond to gas mixture, diagnostics and possible repair come first.
faq.q2: Which gas analyzers can be serviced?
faq.a2: We review portable and fixed gas analyzers for O2, CO, H2S, CH4, and other gases. Provide the model in the request and we will check feasibility.
faq.q3: What documents does the customer receive?
faq.a3: The document set depends on the task and work type. We clarify what is required for operation, internal audit, or inspection in advance.
faq.q4: Can multiple instruments be serviced at once?
faq.a4: Yes. For enterprises, it is usually more convenient to send instruments in batches and maintain a verification schedule.
faq.a5: Verification is performed by an accredited organization. Metris Lab accepts the equipment, performs diagnostics and repair, arranges verification, and supports the order through instrument and document return.
